newsitem.title: USA: Federal judge hands airport win to Chicago.
newsitem.headline: Federal judge hands airport win to Chicago.

text.p: Chicago Mayor Richard Daley got a boost Friday for his plan to transform a small lakefront airport into a bond-financed nature park when a U.S. District Court judge in Chicago rejected a move to temporarily block the plan.

Judge Joan Gottschall denied a motion by a pilots group, plane owners and the state of Illinois to issue a temporary injunction against the city's plans to close Meigs Field on Monday. In her ruling, Gottschall said she did not believe the merits of the lawsuit were strong enough to succeed.
However, an attorney representing the pilots group, said an appeal would be filed with the U.S. Court of Appeals that would also seek a temporary injunction against shutting down the airport.
The Chicago Park District, which owns the airport land, has approved plans to build a $27 million, bond-financed nature park on the site.

Chicago and park district officials said Friday they would postpone plans to dismantle the airport until Wednesday or until the federal appeals court has a chance to decide on the temporary injunction appeal.
